design_name: Banksia-Cork Graded Closed-Cell Radiative-Barrier Heat Shield
inspiration_source: Fire-adapted Banksia serotinous seed follicles and the suberised closed-cell bark of the cork oak (Quercus suber), cross-mapped with vesicular volcanic pumice
physical_mechanism: Semantic features of re-entry: a short intense convective/radiative heat pulse, a surface that must re-radiate, very steep through-thickness temperature gradients, and a structure whose thermal conductivity rises steeply with temperature because in highly porous media radiation across the pores scales as T^3. Cross-domain bridge: bush-fire survivors (Banksia follicles, cork-oak bark) and pumice clasts ejected through hot volcanic plumes solve exactly this problem - protecting a cold interior (seed, cambium, cool core) against a seconds-to-minutes fire pulse using a low-density closed-cell foam with a dense, high-emissivity outer skin. Cork cells are ~20-40 um closed prisms walled with suberin; the tiny cell size suppresses both gas convection and the pore-radiation term (k_rad ~ 4*sigma*d*T^3), while the dense charred skin re-radiates. Translation: a functionally graded closed-cell ceramic/carbon foam with small pores (tens to a few hundred um) and a high-emissivity outer skin. Effective conductivity k(T) = k_s + 4*sigma*d_pore*T^3 (solid + gas conduction plus Rosseland-type pore radiation), which increases roughly an order of magnitude between 300 K and 2000 K. Governing physics: rho*cp*dT/dt = d/dx(k(T) dT/dx) through the thickness, heated by a transient pulse q(t) at the outer face with surface re-radiation, adiabatic inner (bondline) face. Advantage: keeping pores small (cork-like) caps the T^3 radiative leak so the bondline stays cool, and the low density gives low thermal diffusivity at the low-temperature back side where it matters most.

parameters.name: thickness
parameters.justification: Shield thickness L; 3 cm is typical of low-density ablator/foam TPS tiles (PICA, AVCOAT 2-7 cm).

parameters.name: density
parameters.justification: Bulk density of cork (~120-240 kg/m3) and low-density carbon/ceramic foams (~200-500 kg/m3).

parameters.name: specific_heat
parameters.justification: cp of carbon/ceramic foams and cork (~1000-1600 J/kg/K), treated as constant.

parameters.name: solid_conductivity
parameters.justification: Solid+gas conduction contribution k_s (W/m/K); cork ~0.04, PICA virgin ~0.2.

parameters.name: pore_diameter
parameters.justification: Characteristic closed-cell pore size d (m) setting the radiative term 4*sigma*d*T^3; cork cells ~30 um, pumice vesicles up to ~1 mm.

parameters.name: surface_emissivity
parameters.justification: High-emissivity charred / SiC-coated outer skin, analogous to the blackened Banksia follicle surface.

parameters.name: peak_heat_flux
parameters.justification: Peak convective heat flux (W/m2) for LEO return capsules ~0.3-1.5 MW/m2.

parameters.name: pulse_duration
parameters.justification: Duration (s) of the half-sine heating pulse typical of the main re-entry heating phase.

parameters.name: initial_temperature
parameters.justification: Soak temperature (K) of the shield before entry.
